name: answer
program:
# cards: listing
# Six times seven, on a card.
ANSWER
  1   DL 1,1 - TS 2
  3   DL 1,2 - TS 3
  5   MULTIPLY 'A'
  6   TS 4 - TS 13
  8   B, BURY
  9   B, BINDEC
 10   O, DL 10
 11   B, ANSWER 11

DL 1,1   6
DL 1,2   7

name: add
program:
# cards: listing
# Read a card with two numbers on it and punch their sum.
SUM
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 2
  4   ADD 'A'
  5   DL 2,2 - TS 2
  7   ADD
  8   TS 4 - TS 13
 10   B, BURY
 11   B, BINDEC
 12   O, DL 10
 13   B, SUM 13

name: fetch
program:
# Fetch the number whose position is in TS 27, with INDEXIN, and punch it.
FETCH
  1   B, BURY
  2   B, INDEXIN
  3   TS 28 - DL 2,1
  5   O, DL 2
  6   B, FETCH 6

TS 27   DL 3,5
DL 3,5  1945

name: sum-to-n
program:
# cards: listing
# 1 + 2 + ... + n, for the n on the card. TS 20 counts down and TS 21
# holds the total. DISCRIM chooses the way on: back round while TS 20
# still has a digit in it, out when it has none.
TOTAL
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 20
  4   CLEAR TS 21
 10   TS 21 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD;  TS 4 - TS 21
      TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TOTAL 60 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 20
      TS 20 - TS 9;  TS 20 - TS 10;  AND
      TOTAL 61 - TS 15;  TOTAL 62 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
 50   TS 21 - TS 13
 52   B, BURY
 53   B, BINDEC
 54   O, DL 10
 55   B, TOTAL 55
# The numbers: 1, and the two ways on.
 60   +1
 61   B, TOTAL 10
 62   B, TOTAL 50

name: factorial
program:
# cards: listing
# n! for the n on the card, n from 1 to 12. TS 20 counts down from n and
# TS 21 holds the product so far.
FACT
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 20
  4   FACT 60 - TS 21
 10   TS 21 - TS 2;  TS 20 - TS 3;  MULTIPLY 'A';  TS 4 - TS 21
      TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  FACT 60 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 20
      TS 20 - TS 9;  TS 20 - TS 10;  AND
      FACT 61 - TS 15;  FACT 62 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
 50   TS 21 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
 56   B, FACT 56
 60   +1
 61   B, FACT 10
 62   B, FACT 50

name: fibonacci
program:
# cards: listing
# The first n Fibonacci numbers, one card each. TS 20 counts, TS 21 and
# TS 22 are the last two numbers.
FIB
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 20
  4   CLEAR TS 21
  7   FIB 60 - TS 22
 10   TS 22 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
      TS 21 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 22 - TS 2;  ADD
      TS 22 - TS 21;  TS 4 - TS 22
      TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  FIB 60 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 20
      TS 20 - TS 9;  TS 20 - TS 10;  AND
      FIB 61 - TS 15;  FIB 62 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
 58   B, FIB 58
 60   +1
 61   B, FIB 10
 62   B, FIB 58

name: gcd
program:
# cards: listing
# Euclid by subtraction: the greatest common divisor of the two numbers on
# the card. There is no division (section 12 makes it an instruction table
# operation), so the larger is reduced by the smaller until they are equal.
# The sign of a - b is read from TS 5, which is all ones when the partial
# sum is negative, and DISCRIM chooses the way on.
GCD
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 20
  4   DL 2,2 - TS 21
# Equal? a - b has no digit 1.
 10   TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 21 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT
      TS 4 - TS 9;  TS 4 - TS 10;  AND
      GCD 161 - TS 15;  GCD 160 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
# Negative? Then b is the larger.
 40   TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 21 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT
      TS 5 - TS 9;  TS 5 - TS 10;  AND
      GCD 163 - TS 15;  GCD 162 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
# a = a - b
100   TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 21 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 20;  B, GCD 10
# b = b - a
120   TS 21 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 20 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 21;  B, GCD 10
140   TS 20 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
146   B, GCD 146
# The ways on.
160   B, GCD 140
161   B, GCD 40
162   B, GCD 100
163   B, GCD 120

name: polynomial
program:
# cards: listing
# Turing's CALPOL: x^3 - 2x + 5 at x = 7. The sixteen coefficients are in
# DL 3 in pairs, highest power first; the last four are 1, 0, -2, 5.
POLY
  1   B, BURY
  2   B, CALPOL
  3   TS 25 - TS 13
  5   B, BURY
  6   B, BINDEC
  7   O, DL 10
  8   B, POLY 8

TS 13    7
DL 3,25  +1
DL 3,29  -2
DL 3,31  +5

name: indexin-trial
program:
# INDEXIN, printed in section 13, fetches the minor cycle whose position is
# in TS 27 into TS 28. Here it fetches the 1945 kept in DL 3,5 and punches it.
# Tick “Tables as printed” to run INDEXIN exactly as the report prints it.
TRIAL
  1   B, BURY
  2   B, INDEXIN
  3   TS 28 - DL 2,1
  5   O, DL 2
  6   B, TRIAL 6

TS 27   DL 3,5
DL 3,5  1945

name: calpol-twice
program:
# cards: listing
# Turing’s CALPOL twice in a row: x^3 - 2x + 5 at x = 7, which is 334.
# As printed, CALPOL never stops; with four of its five corrections the
# second answer is wrong, because the first call leaves its product behind.
# BINDEC prints what is in TS 13, where CALPOL keeps x, so x is kept in
# DL 1,1 and put back before each call.
TWICE
  1   DL 1,1 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, CALPOL;  TS 25 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
      DL 1,1 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, CALPOL;  TS 25 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
 30   B, TWICE 30

DL 1,1   7
DL 3,25  +1
DL 3,29  -2
DL 3,31  +5

name: blank
program:
# A completely blank instruction has a definite meaning (section 12): pass
# the material on the card in the reader into DL 0. Turing arranged that the
# order the machine starts with is 0 throughout, so that it reads its first
# card without being told.
#
# Here the blank instruction is written as 32 zeros, and the card it reads
# is punched again.
START
  1   0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000
  2   O, DL 0
  3   B, START 3

name: countdown
program:
# cards: listing
# Count down from the number on the card to 1, one card each. The way on is
# chosen by DISCRIM: back round while TS 20 has a digit in it.
COUNT
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 20
 10   TS 20 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
      TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  COUNT 60 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 20
      TS 20 - TS 9;  TS 20 - TS 10;  AND
      COUNT 61 - TS 15;  COUNT 62 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
 50   B, COUNT 50
# The numbers: 1, and the two ways on.
 60   +1
 61   B, COUNT 10
 62   B, COUNT 50

name: echo
program:
# Read a card and punch it again: the smallest job there is. The card goes
# into the first twelve minor cycles of DL 2 and comes out from there.
ECHO
  1   P, DL 2
  2   O, DL 2
  3   B, ECHO 3

name: from-ts6
program:
# An instruction can be obeyed from TS 6 (section 11). B with a 1 in
# column 17 carries out whatever is in TS 6, and if that is of type A the
# machine goes on at the instruction after the B. Here the instruction is
# made by the program: Q puts a position into digits 17-32 of TS 6, and the
# code of type O is added to digits 1-16 by OR. Q leaves digits 1-16 of TS 6
# as they were, so TS 6 is cleared first.
MAKE
  1   NEVER
  2   TS 8 - TS 6
  3   Q, DL 7,1
  4   TS 6 - TS 9
  5   MAKE 20 - TS 10
  7   OR
  8   TS 8 - TS 6
  9   B, 1
 10   B, MAKE 10
# The code of type O, digits 5-8 = 0001.
 20   0000,0001,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000

DL 7,1  +7
DL 7,2  +1

name: logic
program:
# The five logical operations of section 12 work digit by digit on TS 9
# and TS 10 and leave the result in TS 8. Each result is punched as a row
# of the card, so the holes show the digits.
LOGIC
  1   DL 1,1 - TS 9
  3   DL 1,2 - TS 10
  5   AND;   TS 8 - DL 2,1
  8   OR;    TS 8 - DL 2,2
 11   NOT;   TS 8 - DL 2,3
 14   IFF;   TS 8 - DL 2,4
 17   NEVER; TS 8 - DL 2,5
 20   O, DL 2
 21   B, LOGIC 21

DL 1,1  1100,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000
DL 1,2  1010,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000

name: multiply
program:
# cards: listing
# Read two numbers and punch their product. MULTIPLY 'A' is long
# multiplication: TS 2 times TS 3 into the partial sum, which is cancelled
# first. It takes 16 minor cycles, half a millisecond.
PRODUCT
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 2
  4   DL 2,2 - TS 3
  6   MULTIPLY 'A'
  7   TS 4 - TS 13
  9   B, BURY
 10   B, BINDEC
 11   O, DL 10
 12   B, PRODUCT 12

name: negative
program:
# cards: listing
# Numbers are binary, and the last digit has reversed sign: a word of 32
# ones is -1. Subtracting from zero makes a number negative, and BINDEC
# punches the minus sign in row 11.
NEGATE
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 2
  4   SUBTRACT 'A'
  5   TS 4 - TS 13
  7   B, BURY
  8   B, BINDEC
  9   O, DL 10
 10   B, NEGATE 10

name: short-multiplication
program:
# cards: listing
# Short multiplication: a multiplier less than 16 written in the
# instruction itself (GIV), from Fig. 37. S, POS, CANCEL, GIV, 6 is six
# times TS 2. SELF multiplies the partial sum by itself instead, so
# S, POS, CANCEL, SELF, GIV, 6 makes it six times larger again.
SHORT
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 2
  4   S, POS, CANCEL, GIV, 6
  5   S, POS, CANCEL, SELF, GIV, 6
  6   TS 4 - TS 13
  8   B, BURY
  9   B, BINDEC
 10   O, DL 10
 11   B, SHORT 11
